header.name: THEORY AND PRACTICE OF ENGINEERING ETHICS
header.description: The course aims at orienting the students to the theory and practice of meta-ethics, using a multidisciplinary and cross cultural approach. The goal is to help engineering and IT professionals think of ethics as part of the very process of their work. The course does not provide solutions to critical dilemmas. It does not claim to create ‘moral’ people, or ethical engineers. Rather, it encourages critical thinking about ethical issues and decision making. Students will learn to apply meta ethical theories to IT scenarios. We will use a mixed instructional methodology, that includes lecture, discussion, Q&A, one-on-one dialogue, learning team activities, handouts, library reference materials, ppt slides and video clips.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Demonstrate a clear understanding of meta-ethical theories.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Apply meta-ethical theories to engineering and IT scenarios.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Understand the complex ethical paradoxes of IT applications and extensions.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Demonstrate a clear knowledge of the differences between meta-ethics and culturally conditioned moral systems and prescriptions.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Develop a finessed multi-perspectival understanding of moral issues and learn to evaluate moral practices clearly.

lecture_topics: Introduction to the course : Purpose, objectives, scope, methods.
Differences between meta- ethics and social systems of moral practice and prescription.
Why a meta-ethics course is not about producing ‘moral’ people, or ‘good’ engineers.
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Formation of Learning Teams. Assignment 1 : What is the relationship between ethics, morality and law?

lecture_topics: Egoism vs altruism: Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, Gandhi.

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment 2 : Learning team role play, applying what we have learned to engineering scenarios.

lecture_topics: Non-consequentialist theories or deontological theories : Ethics of duty and personhood.
The first and third versions of Kant’s Categorical Imperative.
Kant and the burglar scenario (from Gensler).
Non-consequentialist theories or deontological theories : Ethics of rights and justice

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment 3: Learning team presentation on feminist ethics and theory and gender issues in engineering.
Assignment 4: Learning team presentation on the brands and degrees of relativist and absolutist positions in meta-ethics.

lecture_topics: Applications of ethical theory to technology:: Overview.
Surveillance vs. freedom of expression in the cyber domain.
Freedom of expression vs. ‘the right to be offended’.
Is there such a thing as an ‘ethical’ hacker?
Application of ethical theories discussed, esp. utilitarianism and Kantian ethics.
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment 5: Learning team exercise on freedom vs. surveillance issues.

lecture_topics: Kant, Buber, Levinas and Sherry Turkle: Discussion
The ethics of Social networking: Special focus on Facebook, Twitter, and other popular networking and blogging sites.
Influences on ethical decision making Individual factors
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Assignment 7: Learning teams apply absolutism and relativism to IT scenario of their choice
